note:
ISO 2026-W18 runs from April 27 through May 3. Venus and Uranus are separated by about 3.4° in geocentric ecliptic longitude at the Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot.

**Naked eye:** 🌕 Full Moon · Milk Moon — 17:23:11 UTC. Bright moonlight favors prominent stars and planets while reducing contrast on faint deep-sky objects. No fixed-sky Calendar object is classified for naked-eye observing this week.

**Planets:** Moon: Naked eye; magnitude -11.3; direct motion; 79.2% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Opposition in ecliptic longitude May 01 17:23 UTC. Mercury: In solar glare; magnitude -0.5; direct motion; 81.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Venus: Naked eye; magnitude -3.9; direct motion; 88.9% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Mars: Naked eye; magnitude 1.2; direct motion; 97.9% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Ceres: In solar glare; magnitude 8.8; direct motion; 99.9% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Jupiter: Naked eye; magnitude -2.0; direct motion; 99.2% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Saturn: Naked eye; magnitude 0.9; direct motion; 99.9% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Uranus: Binoculars; magnitude 5.8; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Neptune: Telescope; magnitude 7.8; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Pluto: Substantial telescope; magnitude 14.6; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot.

**Binoculars:** No fixed-sky Calendar object is classified for binocular observing this week.

**Small telescope:** MCG 3-29-20: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; M65: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; NGC 3626: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; M66: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; Arp 317: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; NGC 3766: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; Lambda Centauri Cluster: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance

**Substantial telescope:** No fixed-sky Calendar object is classified as requiring a substantial telescope this week.

descriptors.name: Full Moon
descriptors.summary: Astronomical lunar phase near opposition to the Sun.
descriptors.body: Full Moon is the lunar phase in which the Moon and Sun are approximately opposite in geocentric ecliptic longitude, so the lunar disk is fully illuminated as seen from Earth.

story_candidates.dek: MCG 3-29-20 is an observing target in Leo carried by the weekly Calendar.
story_candidates.body:
Why it is here: The Calendar selected MCG 3-29-20 as one of this week’s fixed-sky observing targets.

How to find it: Establish the preserved Leo constellation figure from its labeled reference stars, then use the target’s plotted position rather than searching for an isolated star.
